negative_reviews.author: Kelsey Beal
negative_reviews.text: Food was okay, noddles great texture but overall wasn't that flavourful, food comes out fast but service is slow. Atmosphere is great

negative_reviews.author: Rashmi Patel
negative_reviews.text: The place looks very nice. The was no atmosphere,  a few people on both sides of us were moaning about the food .... Our instead of timing the food right between the starter and main there was about 5 to 10 mins between that. So we struggles to really enjoy the starters.  And on a small table everything just felt jammed on. We had the pumpkin fritters type things and the gyoza which were nice the pumpkin thing was really nice and worth the money .. I had the seafood hellfire. That were the thought of something nice ended.  The squid was tough and extremely chewy and felt horrible, the broth when I asked what meat is the broth made out of they told me they only use vegetable broth which was disappointing... The thin strips of grilled salmon was nice but due to how thin they were is was very crispy and hard. The prawns were NOT deveined. So I had a mouthful of grit and extras..... The noodle was not nice..... Overall the dish lacked proper flavour. My beautiful wife had  a chicken yakisobi and she experienced a similar result. They automatically add a discretionary service charge. I don't mind actually paying for a good service but a normal standard service should be included. So again I was disappointed.....  After a meal and starter each and 2 drinks we were £70+ light and disappointed.... Never will we return but on good news the post it's on the wall was great and I like the idea.

issues: Covers were 992, down 7 (0.70%) week on week, with big Saturday tables (15, 22, 6, 10 and 7) lifting the total.
Spend per head fell to £20.19, down £0.75 (3.58%).
Sales were £22,448.12, down £1,719.11 (7.11%) week on week and £4,551.88 (16.86%) below the £27,000 target, after a dry spell Monday to Friday, stock issues and low traffic.
Labour was 27.5%, driven up by the freshers fair being cut short by a fire alarm and fewer B2B attendees than expected; Amy Tang has reviewed the rota to bring it down.
Inka Cheung challenged that labour has been high for several weeks while reviews still say service is slow, with five FOH staff and a section plan on Saturdays.

A 3 star Google review said the food was fine but service was slow; the site believes smaller tables were neglected while staff focused on big groups, and the only other Saturday complaint was a steak not cooked medium rare.
Only two people were in the kitchen on Saturday, so a front of house manager had to help in the kitchen and their section may have slowed.
Inka agreed to set strict labour targets aside for four to six weeks so FOH and BOH standards can be retrained, and asked managers to manage by walking the floor.
Food cost is high; the site had misunderstood the reasons and will review invoices, stock and waste with Jason and Ash, including oat milk and matcha waste from B2B drinks.
Substitutions made when items ran out have made stock figures uneven.
At the BOH meeting, beef was reported to have run out on 05/10 with a delivery scheduled, and food cost spiked.
Last week's BOH review complaints were about service speed, with food and ramen quality rated normally.
A sushi chef quit this week; Zula is taking over as sushi manager and a part time kitchen porter is cross-training on sushi.
Binod's last shift is on 07/10.
Delivery was good with low inaccurate orders, but delivery opening hours were 96.7% because the tablet did not switch on automatically on some days, which now seems resolved.
Removal of broken equipment, including the old freezer, is logged as high priority with Francheska and has been chased.
Michael's regional visit gave Leicester a marginal pass because of cleanliness.
Compliance is good and a service is due in two weeks.
For the 06/10 student night the site planned matcha and games rather than food, and could stay open until 10pm if the shopping centre event stays busy.
Restaurant week starts on 19/10.
Labour and sales are the stated areas for improvement.
Region-wide (England): the £5 ramen offer is now limited to one per person through a backend change, announced by Amy Tang at the 06/10 KPI meeting.

Region-wide (England): the Mapal compliance app (transcribed as 'Maple') must be installed on site laptops and iPads, with photos sent to the management chat; front of house staff may no longer use personal phones for compliance on shift, while kitchen staff may use their own phones.

Region-wide (England): table toppers must carry exactly one drink menu, one XOXO drink and one ramen loyalty card, and marketing material requests go to the England group chat for Amy Tang to forward to marketing.

Region-wide (England): at the 06/10 BOH meeting Sophie asked sites to top up stock through the promotions rather than hold back for food cost limits, to monitor dashboard stock levels, and to stop borrowing stock between branches.
